mainTopic: The גיד הנשה on the מזבח, exaggerated language in the words of the חכמים, and רבי יהודה's view that only one thigh is forbidden
overview: The גמרא finishes the debate between רבי and the רבנן on whether the גיד הנשה of a קרבן goes on the מזבח. רבי says an attached גיד הנשה is burned, just like חלב and דם. The רבנן say only what a Jew may eat is offered, and חלב and דם are special because the Torah commands offering them. רב הונא rules that the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and put on the תפוח, the ash pile. He defends this against רב חסדא and a ברייתא, and another ברייתא supports him. Mentioning the תפוח leads to a side discussion about exaggerated language in the Torah, the נביאים and the חכמים, including שמואל's three examples: the תפוח, the golden גפן and the פרוכת. The גמרא then says our משנה, which forbids the גיד in both thighs, does not follow רבי יהודה, who forbids only one thigh. It asks whether רבי יהודה is sure it is the right thigh or only leaning that way. A proof from a משנה about the קרבן פסח is offered, but רב איקא בר חנינא rejects it by explaining the case as one where the two גידים got mixed up.

steps.title: רבי's use of the verse: the attached גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי, no verse is needed for the case already covered. The verse is needed to teach that a גיד הנשה still attached to the meat goes up on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: No verse was needed to include those. The verse was needed for the גיד הנשה while it is still attached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what רבי learns from the verse that says to burn 'all' of the עולה. He says it is about a גיד הנשה that is still attached to the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the permitted parts still attached to the meat (מחוברין דהיתירא) need no verse - they obviously go up with the animal. That leaves the verse 'all' free for a new teaching: even the forbidden גיד הנשה, while still attached, is burned with the rest of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: a verse (a פסוק)
to include, to add something into a law
the sciatic nerve, which a Jew is forbidden to eat
while still attached to the meat

phrases.english: A verse was not needed to include them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the attached permitted parts (מחוברין דהיתירא) - רבי holds they need no verse, since they go up with the animal anyway.

phrases.english: when the verse was needed,
it was for the sciatic nerve while it is attached.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְרַבּוֹיֵי, כִּי אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְגִיד הַנָּשֶׁה בִּמְחוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining רבי's reading of the verse 'all', which began before this text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse 'all' might be needed to include the attached permitted parts.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, the attached permitted parts need no verse, so the verse teaches that an attached גיד הנשה goes up on the מזבח.

steps.title: The רבנן's source: only what a Jew may eat
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from 'ממשקה ישראל' that a קרבן may only come from what is permitted to a Jew. So the forbidden גיד הנשה does not go on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן learn from 'from the drink of Israel' that only what is permitted to Israel may be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the רבנן do not put the גיד הנשה on the מזבח. They bring a verse in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word משקה can mean 'drink', something people consume. The רבנן read the verse to mean that offerings must come from things a Jew is allowed to eat or drink. The גיד הנשה is forbidden to eat, so it may not be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'drink' or 'watering', read here as 'what Israel may consume'
only from what is permitted to a Jew

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: 'From the drink of Israel'
means only from what is permitted to Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view's source against רבי's reading in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן may only come from what a Jew is permitted to eat, so the גיד הנשה is not offered.

steps.title: רבי's answer: just like חלב and דם
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects the רבנן's rule. חלב and דם are forbidden to eat, yet they are offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי says: it is just like forbidden fat and blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes back on the רבנן's verse. He points to forbidden things that clearly do go on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only permitted foods could be offered, then חלב and דם could never be offered. Yet they are offered. So רבי holds that being forbidden to eat does not keep the attached גיד הנשה off the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'just like', used to compare to a known case
forbidden fats of an animal
blood, which is forbidden to eat

phrases.english: And Rabbi says: it is just like forbidden fat and blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rule the רבנן draw in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The general rule that only permitted food may be offered
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חלב and דם are forbidden to eat, yet they are offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: The רבנן's reply: חלב and דם are different
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that חלב and דם are a special case. Offering them is their מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: their מצוה is to be offered this way, so they are different.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן defend their rule against רבי's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah directly commands that חלב and דם be placed on the מזבח, so they are exceptions to the general rule. The Torah never commands offering the גיד הנשה, so it stays under the rule that forbidden food is not offered. This closes the debate between רבי and the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: their מצוה is in this way: they are commanded to be offered
is different, is a special case

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: an attached גיד הנשה goes up on the מזבח, just as חלב and דם do. רבנן: it does not, because only permitted food is offered, and חלב and דם are special since the Torah commands offering them.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: their מצוה is in this way, so they are different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חלב and דם show that forbidden food may be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלב and דם are a special case because the Torah commands offering them. The גיד הנשה has no such command.

steps.title: רב הונא: the גיד הנשה goes on the ash pile
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and placed on the תפוח, the ash pile in the middle of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and put on the ash pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new discussion about the גיד הנשה of an עולה. It opens with רב הונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that the גיד הנשה is not burned together with the rest of the עולה. Instead it is pulled out and set aside on the ash pile. This treats it as something the מזבח should not receive.

keyTerms.meaning: a burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
he pulls it out, removes it
the round pile of ashes in the middle of the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The sciatic nerve of a burnt offering:
one removes it and puts it on the ash pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה שֶׁל עוֹלָה חוֹלְצוֹ לַתַּפּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on the same topic, the גיד הנשה and the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and placed on the תפוח.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the Torah only forbids Jews from eating it
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges רב הונא. The verse forbids the גיד הנשה only to the people of Israel, not to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Master of this ruling! Does it say 'therefore the altar shall not eat'? It says 'therefore the children of Israel shall not eat'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רב הונא's ruling by looking closely at the wording of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's ban on the גיד הנשה speaks only about the children of Israel eating it. The מזבח is not mentioned. So רב חסדא sees no reason to remove the גיד הנשה from the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'master of this', a sharp call aimed at the one who gave the ruling
'is it written...?', a challenge from the exact words of a verse
the altar

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא does not mean the מזבח 'eats' in a literal sense. He is reading the verse closely to show that the ban is only on Jews eating it, not on offering it.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: Master of this ruling!
phrases.notes: He is speaking to the author of the ruling, רב הונא.

phrases.aramaic: מִי כְּתִיב ״עַל כֵּן לֹא יֹאכַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״?
phrases.english: Is it written: 'Therefore the altar shall not eat'?

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל כֵּן לֹא יֹאכְלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ כְּתִיב.
phrases.english: It is written: 'Therefore the children of Israel shall not eat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִי דֵּיכִי, מִי כְּתִיב ״עַל כֵּן לֹא יֹאכַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed to the תפוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse forbids the גיד הנשה only to Jews eating it, not to the מזבח, so there is no reason to remove it from the עולה.

steps.title: רב הונא's source: only what is permitted to a Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers רב חסדא: he learns from 'ממשקה ישראל' that a קרבן comes only from what is permitted to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא holds that 'ממשקה ישראל' means: only from what is permitted to a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא is not bothered by רב חסדא's question. He has his own פסוק showing the forbidden גיד הנשה cannot be burned on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the verse forbids the גיד הנשה only to people, not to the מזבח. רב הונא answers with the same source the רבנן used: 'ממשקה ישראל' teaches that only food a Jew may eat can be offered. Since the גיד הנשה is forbidden to eat, it cannot be burned as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the well-watered pastures of Israel' (יחזקאל 45:15), the source for which animals and parts may be offered
From what a Jew is allowed to eat
The sciatic nerve, which a Jew may not eat

phrases.english: And Rav Huna holds: 'From the well-watered pastures of Israel'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק the רבנן used in step 2.

phrases.english: means: from what is permitted to Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge in step 6 by giving רב הונא's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supplying a different פסוק as the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא seemed to have no reason to keep the גיד הנשה off the מזבח, since the verse forbids it only to people.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא relies on 'ממשקה ישראל': what a Jew may not eat may not be offered.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say the nerve of an עולה is burned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the גיד הנשה of an עולה is 'brought up', which seems to mean it is burned on the מזבח, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: the גיד הנשה of a שלמים is swept to the drain, and of an עולה, one brings it up. Doesn't that mean he brings it up and burns it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא. 'He brings it up' sounds like the nerve is burned on the מזבח together with the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a שלמים, the meat is eaten, so the forbidden nerve is simply thrown away into the drain. With an עולה, the ברייתא says something different: 'he brings it up.' The simple reading is that it goes up and is burned with the whole animal, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering, most of which is eaten
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
The water channel running through the Temple courtyard
He burns it on the מזבח
'Isn't it that...?', proposing a reading that creates a problem

phrases.english: They raised an objection: the sciatic nerve of a peace offering —
one sweeps it to the drain,
and that of a burnt offering — one brings it up.
phrases.notes: 'Brings it up' means up onto the מזבח.

phrases.english: Is it not that he brings it up and burns it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling, which step 7 had just defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and put on the תפוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the nerve of an עולה is 'brought up', which seems to mean burned on the מזבח.

steps.title: It goes up only to be removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the nerve is brought up and then removed, not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, he brings it up and removes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading in step 8. 'He brings it up' means the leg goes up with the nerve, and then the nerve is pulled out on top of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never said 'burns it'. The nerve goes up while still in the leg, but it is taken out before the leg is put on the fire. So the ברייתא agrees with רב הונא after all.

keyTerms.meaning: He removes it (pulls the nerve out of the leg)
He brings it up onto the מזבח

phrases.english: No, he brings it up and removes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He brings it up' means it is burned on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is brought up inside the leg and then removed on top, not burned.

steps.title: Why bring it up if it will be removed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the nerve is going to be removed anyway, why bring it up at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since he removes it, why does he bring it up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. It is setting up the next step, which will explain why the nerve goes up first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nerve is not burned, it seems simpler to take it out below and bring up only the leg. The גמרא wants to know why the ברייתא bothers to have it brought up.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; given that
Why

phrases.english: And since he removes it, why does he bring it up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of the answer in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the nerve goes up onto the מזבח if it will just be removed.

steps.title: Don't bring God a damaged gift
steps.stepSummary: The leg must go up whole, because מלאכי teaches that one may not offer something damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says: 'Present it now to your governor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 10. Taking the nerve out below would bring a cut-up, damaged leg to the מזבח, which is disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prophet complains that people bring God gifts they would never dare give a human governor. So the leg is brought up whole and looking proper, and only then is the nerve removed on top of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Present it now to your governor', meaning: would you give a damaged gift to a human ruler?
Governor
Because it is stated, introducing a פסוק as the reason

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that respect for the מזבח matters even in how a part is removed, not only in what is burned.

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
'Present it now to your governor.'
phrases.notes: מלאכי 1:8. Taking the nerve out first would leave the leg looking damaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leg goes up whole so a damaged-looking offering is not brought; the nerve is removed on top.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא clearly says the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and placed on the תפוח, just like רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב הונא: the גיד הנשה of a שלמים is swept to the drain, and that of an עולה is removed and placed on the תפוח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב הונא said. This backs up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא matches the first one about the שלמים. For the עולה, instead of the unclear 'brings it up', it says plainly that the nerve is removed and put on the ash pile. That is רב הונא's ruling word for word.

keyTerms.meaning: In agreement with him
The round ash pile in the middle of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The גיד הנשה of an עולה goes up on the leg, is removed on top, and is placed on the תפוח, not burned. This is because 'ממשקה ישראל' teaches that only what a Jew may eat is offered.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Huna:
the sciatic nerve of a peace offering —
one sweeps it to the drain,
and that of a burnt offering — one removes it to the ash mound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא, the גמרא brings direct support for him.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that the גיד הנשה of an עולה is removed and put on the תפוח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'ושל עולה חולצו לתפוח'

steps.title: The ash pile on the altar was huge, but the number is an exaggeration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה saying the תפוח sometimes held three hundred כור of ashes. רבא says this is a גוזמא, an exaggeration.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: There was an ash pile in the middle of the altar, and sometimes it held about three hundred כור. רבא said: That is an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step mentioned the תפוח, so the גמרא now brings a משנה that describes how big it got. רבא says the number is not meant literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three hundred כור is an enormous amount, far too much to sit on the מזבח. רבא explains that the משנה only means the pile was very large. This step opens a side discussion about exaggerated language.

keyTerms.meaning: The round pile of ashes in the middle of the מזבח
The altar in the בית המקדש
A very large measure of volume
An exaggeration; not meant literally

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת תמיד.

phrases.english: There was an ash pile in the middle of the altar.
Sometimes there was on it
about three hundred כור.
רבא said: It is an exaggeration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The תפוח mentioned in step 12 leads the גמרא into a side discussion about a משנה that describes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's figure of three hundred כור is an exaggeration, according to רבא.

steps.title: The golden cup for the תמיד is also an exaggeration
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the תמיד lamb was given water from a golden cup. רבא again says this is an exaggeration.
steps.simpleTranslation: They gave the תמיד water to drink from a golden cup. רבא said: That is an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה that רבא also calls an exaggeration. It is adding another example of the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the lamb drinking from a gold cup. רבא says this did not really happen and is just a fancy way of describing the event. Now there are two examples of exaggeration in the words of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily קרבן offered every morning and afternoon
They gave to drink
A cup made of gold

phrases.english: They gave the תמיד to drink
from a cup of gold.
רבא said: It is an exaggeration.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִשְׁקוּ אֶת הַתָּמִיד בְּכוֹס שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second example, alongside step 13, of רבא calling a משנה an exaggeration.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The golden cup in the משנה is an exaggeration, according to רבא.

steps.title: Torah, נביאים and חכמים all use exaggerated language
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי states a general rule: the Torah, the נביאים and the חכמים sometimes speak in exaggerated language.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: The Torah spoke in exaggerated language, the נביאים spoke in exaggerated language, and the חכמים spoke in exaggerated language.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי turns רבא's two examples into a broad rule. This sets up the proofs that come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's comments were about two specific משניות. רבי אמי widens the idea to cover all three levels of our sources. Some descriptions are written to show how great something was, not to give an exact measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: Exaggerated language; wording used for effect
The Prophets; the books of נביאים
The Sages of the משנה and the ברייתות

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean anything in the Torah can be dismissed as exaggeration. רבי אמי gives specific descriptive examples that are obviously not literal, such as walls reaching the sky.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
The Torah spoke in exaggerated language,
the Prophets spoke in exaggerated language,
the Sages spoke in exaggerated language.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה לְשׁוֹן הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This widens רבא's two specific comments into a general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah, the נביאים and the חכמים all sometimes use exaggerated language.

steps.title: Examples of exaggeration from the חכמים, the Torah and the נביאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves each part of רבי אמי's rule. For the חכמים, it points to the examples just given. For the Torah, it cites cities fortified 'up to the heavens.' For the נביאים, it cites the earth splitting from the people's noise.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים spoke in exaggerated language: that is what we just said. The Torah spoke in exaggerated language: 'cities great and fortified up to the heavens.' The נביאים spoke in exaggerated language: 'and the earth split from their sound.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up each of the three parts of רבי אמי's statement with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof for the חכמים is the two משניות רבא already explained. The Torah's walls did not really reach the sky, and the ground did not really split at שלמה's coronation. These descriptions just mean 'very tall' and 'very loud.'

keyTerms.meaning: That which we already said
Fortified; walled
And it split open

steps.whatToRemember: Some descriptions in the Torah, the נביאים and the משנה are exaggerations meant to show greatness: the 300 כור ash pile, the golden cup, walls up to the sky, and the earth splitting from noise.

phrases.english: The Sages spoke in exaggerated language:
that which we just said.
phrases.notes: He means the 300 כור ash pile and the golden cup from steps 13 and 14.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in exaggerated language:
"cities great and fortified up to the heavens"
The Prophets spoke in exaggerated language:
"and the earth split from their sound."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים לְשׁוֹן הֲוַאי – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the proofs for each part of רבי אמי's rule in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's rule that the Torah, the נביאים and the חכמים all use exaggerated language
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משניות about the תפוח and the golden cup, דברים 9:1, and מלכים א 1:40

steps.title: שמואל lists three places where the Sages exaggerated
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the חכמים used exaggerated language in three places: the תפוח, the גפן and the פרוכת. The תפוח was already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: In three places the חכמים spoke in exaggerated language: the ash pile, the vine and the Curtain. The ash pile is the case we already mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a list of exactly three places where the חכמים exaggerated. The first one, the תפוח, is the case we already saw, and the גמרא is setting up to explain the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said in general that the חכמים sometimes exaggerate. שמואל goes further and names three specific cases. The תפוח holding three hundred כור was already called a גוזמא by רבא, so no new source is needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Exaggerated language; describing something as bigger than it really was
The round pile of ashes in the middle of the מזבח
Vine; here, a golden ornament shaped like a vine
The Curtain separating the היכל from the קודש הקדשים

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani says that Shmuel says:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת דִּבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים לְשׁוֹן הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: In three places the Sages spoke in exaggerated language,
and they are: the ash mound, the vine, and the Curtain.
The ash mound: that is what we already said.
phrases.notes: He means the משנה from step 13 that said the pile sometimes held three hundred כור of ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת דִּבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים לְשׁוֹן הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי אמי's general rule about exaggeration into a specific list of three cases from the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים exaggerated in exactly three places: the תפוח, the גפן, and the פרוכת.

steps.title: The golden vine moved by three hundred priests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the golden גפן at the entrance of the היכל, which three hundred כהנים were needed to move.
steps.simpleTranslation: The vine is what we learned in a משנה: A golden vine stood at the entrance of the היכל, spread over poles. Anyone who donated a golden grape or cluster would bring it and hang it on the vine. רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק said: Once three hundred כהנים were assigned to move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the second exaggeration on שמואל's list. It is the claim that three hundred כהנים were needed to move the golden vine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vine kept growing because people kept adding golden grapes and clusters to it. The number 'three hundred כהנים' is the part שמואל calls exaggerated. It means the vine was very heavy, not that exactly three hundred people carried it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש
Poles or beams that the vine was spread over
A single grape (here, made of gold)
A cluster of grapes

phrases.english: The vine: as we learned in a mishna:
A vine of gold was standing
at the entrance of the Sanctuary,
trained up on top of poles,
and whoever would donate
a grape or a cluster
would bring it and hang it on the vine.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק: מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said: There was an incident,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְנוּ עָלֶיהָ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת כֹּהֲנִים לְפַנּוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: and three hundred priests were assigned to it to move it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the second item on שמואל's list.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that the גפן is described with exaggeration
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מדות about the golden vine, with רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's report of three hundred כהנים

steps.title: The huge Curtain immersed by three hundred priests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה describing the פרוכת: a טפח thick, very costly, made twice a year, and immersed by three hundred כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Curtain is what we learned in a משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said in the name of רבי שמעון הסגן: The Curtain is a handbreadth thick. It is woven of seventy-two strands, and each strand has twenty-four threads. It is forty אמות long and twenty אמות wide. It costs eight hundred twenty thousand, two are made each year, and three hundred כהנים immerse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the third exaggeration on שמואל's list, the description of the פרוכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives very large numbers for the פרוכת's thickness, cost and weight. The גמרא does not say which detail שמואל means. A likely candidate is the three hundred כהנים needed to immerse it, the same number used for the גפן, but the thickness or the other figures may also be meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a measure of about the width of a hand
Strands of yarn woven together
Ten thousand
Immersing in a מקוה to make it טהור

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's three exaggerations: the תפוח (three hundred כור of ashes), the גפן (three hundred כהנים to move it), and the פרוכת (its huge measurements; the גמרא does not say which detail is exaggerated).

phrases.english: The Curtain: as we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַסְּגָן –
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Shimon the deputy High Priest:
The Curtain's thickness is a handbreadth,
and it is woven from seventy-two strands,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כׇּל נִימָה וְנִימָה עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חוּטִין.
phrases.english: and each and every strand has twenty-four threads.

phrases.aramaic: אׇרְכָּהּ אַרְבָּעִים בָּאַמָּה, וְרׇחְבָּהּ עֶשְׂרִים בְּאַמָּה,
phrases.english: Its length is forty cubits, and its width is twenty cubits,
and it is made from eighty-two ten-thousands,
and they make two each year,
and three hundred priests immerse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the third and last item on שמואל's list, closing the topic of exaggerations.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that the פרוכת is described with exaggeration
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים quoting רבי שמעון הסגן

steps.title: Our משנה, both thighs, does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'in the right thigh and in the left thigh' and says this does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'in the right thigh and in the left thigh.' Our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes our משנה, which says גיד הנשה is forbidden in both thighs, and says this is not the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the איסור applies to both legs. The גמרא points out that this is not everyone's view. It is about to bring the source showing that רבי יהודה disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Thigh, where the גיד הנשה is found
Our משנה
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין וּבְיָרֵךְ שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל.
phrases.english: The mishna said: In the thigh of the right and in the thigh of the left.
Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the exaggeration discussion and returns to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling that the איסור applies to both thighs is not like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says only one thigh, probably the right
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה holds the איסור of גיד הנשה applies to only one thigh, and logic says it is the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says it applies only to one thigh, and logic says it is the right one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רבי יהודה disagrees with our משנה. He holds the איסור is only in one thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה forbids the גיד in both thighs. רבי יהודה forbids it in only one, and says reasoning points to the right thigh. Whether he means he is certain or only leaning that way is the question the גמרא asks in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It applies only to one (thigh)
Logic decides; reasoning points to this answer

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה: גיד הנשה is forbidden in both thighs. רבי יהודה: only one thigh, and logic points to the right.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'logic decides' (הדעת מכרעת) are unclear: they could mean a firm Torah reasoning or just a leaning. The גמרא raises exactly this question in the next step.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
It applies only in one thigh,
and logic decides that it is the right one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 20 that our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה is not like רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה limits the איסור to one thigh

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה certain or unsure about the right thigh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה is sure the איסור is on the right thigh (דעת תורה), or is in doubt and only leaning toward the right (דעת נוטה).
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is it clear to רבי יהודה that it is the right thigh, so that 'logic' means the logic of the Torah? Or is he really in doubt, so that 'logic' means logic leans that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה meant by the word 'logic' (דעת) when he said the forbidden גיד is in the right thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read him. Either he is fully sure, based on the Torah's own reasoning, that only the right thigh is forbidden. Or he does not know which thigh it is and only leans toward the right, which would leave both thighs in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is completely clear and obvious to him
He is truly in doubt
The logic of the Torah, a firm conclusion
Logic leans that way, a hunch and not certainty

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree רבי יהודה says only one thigh is forbidden. The question is only whether he knows for sure which one.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is it clear and obvious to Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: Clear that the forbidden גיד is the one in the right thigh, as in the ברייתא of step 21.

phrases.english: and what does 'logic' mean? The logic of the Torah,
or perhaps he is in doubt,
and what does 'logic' mean? Logic leans that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the word 'logic' in the ברייתא of רבי יהודה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה is certain that only the right thigh is forbidden, or is in doubt and only leaning that way.

steps.title: A משנה about burning bones, sinews and leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in פסחים: the bones, sinews and נותר of the קרבן פסח are burned on the sixteenth of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The bones, the sinews and the leftover meat should be burned on the sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts building a proof from a משנה about the קרבן פסח. This step only sets up the source. The proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists 'sinews' as something that must be burned, separate from leftover meat. The גמרא will ask which sinews these could be, and that answer will settle the question about רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover meat of a קרבן past its time, which must be burned
They are burned on the sixteenth of ניסן, not on יום טוב
Sinews

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in פסחים 83a about the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: The bones, the sinews, and the leftover meat
should be burned on the sixteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה is certain or in doubt about which thigh is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פסחים 83a about burning the bones, sinews and נותר of the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: Which sinews could need burning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier discussion: meat sinews should be eaten, leftover ones are already נותר, and neck sinews that are not meat should just be thrown away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What is the case of these sinews? If they are meat sinews, let him eat them. If they were left over, that is just נותר. Rather, they are neck sinews. But if they are not meat, let him throw them away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back an earlier question on that משנה: no kind of sinew seems to fit the משנה's need to burn 'sinews.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Edible sinews are simply eaten. If they were not eaten in time, they are already included in 'נותר.' Inedible neck sinews are not meat at all, so there is no reason to burn them. This difficulty sets up רב חסדא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: We discussed it, recalling an earlier discussion
Neck sinews, which are not counted as meat
Let him throw them away

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
These sinews, what is their case?
If they are sinews of meat, let him eat them,
and if they were left over, that is the same as leftover meat!
Rather, they are neck sinews,
but if they are not meat, let him throw them away?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: הָנֵי גִּידֵי מַאי עֲבִידְתַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case of 'sinews' the משנה from step 23 could mean.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of sinews as something to be burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every kind of sinew is either eaten, already included in נותר, or not meat and simply thrown away. None of them needs its own mention as something to burn.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it means the גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה is talking about the גיד הנשה, following רבי יהודה, who holds that only one thigh's גיד is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: It is only needed for the גיד הנשה, and according to רבי יהודה, who said it applies only to one thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא solves the difficulty: the sinews in the משנה are the גידי הנשה, following רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, one of the two גידים is permitted meat and the other is forbidden. That creates a special case of sinews that cannot be eaten yet still need burning. The next step explains why this only works if he is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
It was only needed for, introducing the specific case meant
According to the view of

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
It is needed only for the sciatic nerve,
and according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: it applies only to one thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְגִיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 24 by naming the specific sinews.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case of the משנה as the גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No kind of sinew should need burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means the גידי הנשה according to רבי יהודה, who forbids only one of them.

steps.title: So רבי יהודה must be in doubt
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's answer works only if רבי יהודה is unsure which thigh is forbidden. If he were sure, the permitted גיד would be eaten and the forbidden one thrown away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say he is in doubt, it works out well. But if you say it is obvious to him, then the permitted one, let him eat it, and the forbidden one, let him throw it away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof: since the משנה requires burning the sinews, רבי יהודה must be in doubt about which thigh is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is in doubt, neither גיד may be eaten. Each one might be the permitted one, which has now become leftover meat, so both must be burned. If he were certain, nothing would need burning: the permitted גיד is eaten and the forbidden one is simply thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say, meaning this side works
It works out well
The permitted one
The forbidden one

steps.whatToRemember: The proposed proof: the משנה's requirement to burn the sinews seems to show that רבי יהודה is in doubt (דעת נוטה). The next step rejects this proof.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
he is in doubt, it works out well,
but if you say
it is clear and obvious to him,
the permitted one, let him eat it,
the forbidden one, let him throw it away!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב חסדא's answer to settle the question of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is in doubt (דעת נוטה) about which thigh is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פסחים requiring the sinews to be burned, as explained by רב חסדא.

steps.title: The two גידים were known, then mixed up
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בר חנינא rejects the proof. רבי יהודה can be certain it is the right thigh, and the משנה is about גידים that were identified and later got mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא בר חנינא said: Really, I can tell you that רבי יהודה is completely sure which thigh is forbidden. The משנה is dealing with a case where the גידים were first identified, and only afterward they got mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב איקא בר חנינא pushes back on the proof from Step 26. He shows that the משנה can still fit even if רבי יהודה is fully sure about the right thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof said: if רבי יהודה were sure, we would eat the permitted גיד and throw out the forbidden one, so there would be nothing to burn. רב איקא answers that the doubt can come from the facts, not from רבי יהודה's opinion. Once the right and left גידים get mixed, nobody knows which one may be eaten, so both are left over and burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. This word signals that we keep the original position and explain the source a different way.
It is completely clear to him, meaning he is certain (the opposite of being in doubt).
"What case are we dealing with here?" This phrase introduces a specific case that makes the source fit.
They were identified, meaning it was known which גיד came from which thigh.
They became mixed together.

steps.whatToRemember: The proof falls away. The משנה can be explained even if רבי יהודה is sure, because the doubt comes from the גידים getting mixed up, not from רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב איקא is saying רבי יהודה is unsure. He says the opposite: רבי יהודה is sure. The doubt in the משנה is only about which physical גיד is which after they got mixed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא pushes back on a proof: it explains the source as a special case, so the source no longer proves the point.

phrases.english: Rav Ika bar Ḥanina said:
Actually, I can say to you
that it is completely clear to him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יהודה. He is sure it is the right thigh's גיד that is forbidden.

phrases.english: and what case are we dealing with here?
where they were identified
phrases.notes: "They" are the two גידים of the פסח, the right one and the left one.

phrases.english: and in the end they became mixed together.

steps.triggerLanguage: לעולם אימא לך מיפשט פשיטא ליה והכא במאי עסקינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 26 by explaining the משנה as a case of identified-then-mixed גידים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסח משנה. It does not prove that רבי יהודה is sure. It only shows the משנה works either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the only possible reason to burn both גידים is that רבי יהודה himself is unsure. But a mix-up of the actual גידים also creates doubt, even if רבי יהודה is certain.
